recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-11534 unless a future work-group decision changes the ActivityDefinition/Task boundary.
issue_request: FHIR-11534 was a Published/Persuasive CDS change request asking the specification to clarify why ActivityDefinition differs from Task. The accepted resolution said ActivityDefinition describes what should be done in the abstract, while Task represents actionable portions of a concrete activity as it moves through workflow.
initial_application: Git/SVN commit c03a8aca8404dc242356064fbc17b482dfc33d81, SVN 10927, explicitly listed #11534 and added a Boundaries and Relationships paragraph to source/activitydefinition/activitydefinition-introduction.xml. Later commit bd1507dafa96568bf37503ff029bbabe8c3d8be2 updated workflow links and nearby wording while preserving the ActivityDefinition-versus-Task distinction.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively includes task=Task, activitydefinition=ActivityDefinition, and ActivityDefinition=adf, confirming build scope. Current ActivityDefinition narrative still states that ActivityDefinition represents the description of a task in the abstract while Task tracks a specific task instance through workflow steps. Current Task source describes workflow inputs, outputs, and execution progress. FHIR-12415 is a related no-change tracker whose resolution relies on ActivityDefinition.kind supporting any resource type and does not change this boundary. Zulip and Confluence searches found no direct FHIR-11534 discussion or conflicting later work-group record.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch because the current build-scoped source already implements the accepted clarification.

related_jiras.note: Related Task/ActivityDefinition use-case was resolved no-change by relying on ActivityDefinition.kind support for any resource type, without altering the ActivityDefinition-versus-Task boundary.
